Palpable

PAL-puh-bul -- shares a root with 'palpitate,' meaning to touch or feel. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Palpable is able to be touched or felt; so obvious it seems almost touchable.

As the jury filed back into the courtroom, the tension in the room was palpable.

Worked Example

The instant the results are announced, silence grips the entire stadium so completely that you could almost reach out and touch the disappointment in the air.

That sense of an emotion being so strong it feels almost physical is exactly what palpable describes. Unlike 'subtle,' which is easy to miss, palpable is impossible to ignore.

How Palpable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tangible

tangible: able to be perceived clearly, almost as if touched

unmistakable

unmistakable: so clear it cannot be mistaken for anything else

evident

evident: clearly visible or obvious

Antonyms

imperceptible

imperceptible: impossible to notice or sense

intangible

intangible: unable to be touched or clearly grasped

How Strong Is It? — evident → tangible → palpable

evident vs. palpable

evident vs. palpable: Evident is a bit milder than palpable -- evident just means clearly visible, while palpable adds the sense that a feeling is so strong it seems almost physical.

tangible vs. palpable

tangible vs. palpable: Tangible can feel closer to the word's literal root than palpable: both suggest something is nearly touchable, though tangible is used more broadly for concrete facts and results, not just emotions in a room.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — -palp-

root — -palp-: to touch, stroke gently (Latin (palpare))

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: able to be, capable of being (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin palpare meant 'to touch or stroke gently,' and adding -able ('able to be') gives 'able to be touched.' Something palpable feels so real and present you could almost put your hand on it -- the same root gives us palpitate.

Use the root in a new word: palpitate

Use the root in a new word: palpitate: Her heart began to palpitate the moment she heard footsteps behind her in the empty hallway.
